notes.objective: Know the licence ladder and test sequence
notes.title: From learner to Class 2B, 2A and 2
notes.gist: Class 2B is the starting motorcycle licence. You pass the BTT, get a PDL, pass the RTT, then pass the practical within a year of the RTT.
points: Class 2B: petrol below 200cc, electric below 15 kW.
Class 2A: 200 to 400cc or 15 to 25 kW, after holding 2B for at least one year.
Class 2: above 400cc or above 25 kW, after holding 2A for at least one year.
PDL after the BTT, valid 2 years. Eyesight: 6 characters and red, amber, green at 25 m.
RTT pass valid one year. Miss the practical in that window and you retake the RTT.
After the practical, the 100-minute Expressway Familiarisation Ride is compulsory before the licence.
notes.tip: Traps mix up the FTT (cars) and RTT (motorcycles), and the RTT validity: it is one year, not two.
notes.diagram:
flowchart TB
  A[Class 2B: below 200cc or 15 kW] -->|hold 1 year| B[Class 2A: 200 to 400cc]
  B -->|hold 1 year| C[Class 2: above 400cc]

notes.objective: Apply the probation and demerit point rules
notes.title: Probation and DIPS demerit points
notes.gist: New riders are on probation for a year and lose the licence at 13 points. Later, 24 points in 24 months brings a first suspension.
points: Probation Plate front and rear: above or below the headlamp and the rear number plate.
Two offences of not showing the plate during probation: licence revoked.
13 or more points during probation: new licence revoked.
First suspension: 24 or more points within 24 months, 12 weeks.
With a past suspension: 12 or more points within 12 months.
12 months free of offences clears all demerit points.
notes.tip: Know the speeding ladder: up to 20 over is 6 points, 21 to 30 is 8, 31 to 40 is 12, above 40 is court. Red light is 12.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  N[New rider, year 1] -->|13 points| R[Licence revoked]
  O[Experienced rider] -->|24 points in 24 months| S[12 week suspension]
  S -->|12 points in 12 months| S2[Next suspension]
  O -->|12 months clean| Z[Points cleared]

source.title: Basic Theory of Driving, DIPS

notes.objective: Know the key riding laws
notes.title: Alcohol, helmets, phones and modifications
notes.gist: The laws riders are most often tested on: alcohol limits, helmet use, handheld phones and illegal modifications.
points: Alcohol limit: 80 mg per 100 ml of blood, or 35 micrograms per 100 ml of breath.
You can be charged even below the limit if you are not in proper control.
Rider and pillion must wear an approved, fastened helmet. Only turbaned male Sikhs are exempt.
Phone offence: holding it, using any function, while moving. Hands-free is fine.
Illegal modification: fine up to $2,000 or up to 6 months in jail. Check LTA rules first.
Third-party insurance is the legal minimum.
notes.tip: Blood is milligrams, breath is micrograms: 80 and 35. Swapping the units is the classic distractor.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  H[Hand holds device] --> X{All three true?}
  F[Using any function] --> X
  M[Vehicle moving] --> X
  X -->|yes| OFF[Offence]
  X -->|no| OK[Not this offence]

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, mobile devices

summary.tests: Whether you know the licence classes and test order, the probation and DIPS rules, and the core laws on alcohol, helmets, phones and modifications.
must_know: Class 2B is below 200cc petrol or below 15 kW electric.
BTT, then PDL, then RTT, then the practical within one year of the RTT.
Probation lasts one year: 13 points or two missing-plate offences revokes the licence.
First suspension at 24 points in 24 months, 12 weeks long.
Alcohol limits are 80 mg per 100 ml of blood and 35 micrograms per 100 ml of breath.
Helmet offence and excess pillion offence are each 3 points.
Red light 12 points. Speeding 6, 8, 12 points, then court above 40 km/h over.
traps: Saying the RTT is valid two years: it is one year.
Thinking a hands-free headset is an offence: only holding and using the device while moving is.
Assuming you cannot be charged below the alcohol limit.

cards.q: What engine size does a Class 2B licence cover?
cards.a: Petrol motorcycles below 200cc, or electric motorcycles below 15 kW.

cards.q: How long must you hold Class 2B before taking the Class 2A test?
cards.a: At least one year.

cards.q: How long is an RTT pass valid?
cards.a: One year. Pass the practical within it or retake the RTT.

cards.q: How long is a PDL valid?
cards.a: Two years from the date of grant, renewable every two years.

cards.q: What demerit total revokes a probationary rider's licence?
cards.a: 13 or more points within the one-year probation.

cards.q: Where does the Probation Plate go on a Class 2B motorcycle?
cards.a: Above or below the headlamp, and above or below the rear licence plate.

cards.q: When is a first suspension triggered under DIPS?
cards.a: 24 or more demerit points within 24 months. It lasts 12 weeks.

cards.q: What are the blood and breath alcohol limits?
cards.a: 80 mg per 100 ml of blood; 35 micrograms per 100 ml of breath.

cards.q: Who is exempt from the motorcycle helmet law?
cards.a: Male Sikhs wearing a turban.

cards.q: Demerit points for riding without a helmet or with it unfastened?
cards.a: 3 points.

cards.q: Demerit points for speeding by 20 km/h or less?
cards.a: 6 points. 21 to 30 over is 8, 31 to 40 over is 12.

cards.q: Demerit points for beating a red light?
cards.a: 12 points, with a $400 to $500 fine.

cards.q: Three conditions for the mobile device offence?
cards.a: A hand holds the device, you use any function, and the vehicle is moving.

cards.q: Penalty for unauthorised vehicle modification?
cards.a: A fine up to $2,000 or up to 6 months' jail.

cards.q: How do zone offences in School and Silver Zones and Friendly Streets change penalties?
cards.a: Plus 2 demerit points and plus $100 on the fine, capped at $500.

notes.objective: Recognise rider conditions that make riding unsafe
notes.title: Your eyes, body and mind
notes.gist: About 80% of riding information comes through the eyes, and tiredness, emotion, alcohol and drugs all slow perception and reaction.
points: Riding is a chain of perception, judgement and reaction; most crashes come from poor perception and judgement.
Keep your eyes moving about every two seconds; your field of vision narrows as speed rises.
Do not ride when tired, giddy, unwell, angry or worried.
Check with your doctor whether medicine causes drowsiness.
Tiredness and alcohol increase reaction time.
notes.tip: If a question asks what to do when tired or unwell, the answer is do not ride, not ride slowly.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  P[Perception] --> J[Judgement] --> R[Reaction]
  T[Tired, angry, alcohol] -.->|slows| P
  T -.->|slows| R

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, human factors

notes.objective: Choose correct protective gear and posture
notes.title: Gear up and sit right
notes.gist: Most rider injuries are to the chest and limbs, so wear full protective gear, and use a posture that gives quick control and less fatigue.
points: Approved helmet with the chin strap fastened; white helmet and reflective clothing at night.
Replace a badly scratched visor: it causes glare and dazzle.
Bright, tear-resistant clothing; no baggy or flared trousers.
Proper boots, never sandals or slippers; avoid loose laces.
Posture: look far ahead, elbows slightly bent about 120 degrees, sit close to the tank, light knee grip.
Feet on the footrest arches, covering the gear lever and brake pedal.
notes.tip: Looking at the front wheel is always wrong: it upsets your balance. Look far ahead.
notes.diagram:
flowchart TB
  E[Eyes far ahead] --> B[Good balance]
  S[Shoulders relaxed, elbows bent] --> Q[Quick control]
  K[Knees grip tank] --> B
  F[Feet cover pedals] --> Q
  B --> L[Less fatigue]
  Q --> L

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, riding wear and posture

notes.objective: Perform pre-riding and weekly checks
notes.title: The numbers in the checks
notes.gist: Pre-riding checks take minutes and come before every ride; weekly checks go deeper. The test asks for the specific figures.
points: Tyre tread: replace below 1.6 mm. Uneven pressure upsets hard braking.
Chain slack: about 20 mm. A loose chain can come off and lock the rear wheel.
Brake lever and pedal free play: 15 to 20 mm.
Clutch lever free play: 10 to 20 mm.
Engine oil: check cold, upright, on flat ground; dipstick inserted without screwing in.
Mirrors: tip of your shoulder at the lower edge; do not adjust on the main stand.
notes.tip: Brakes 15 to 20, clutch 10 to 20, chain 20, tread 1.6: memorise these four numbers.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  W[Weekly check] --> O[Oil level cold and upright]
  W --> CH[Chain 20 mm slack]
  W --> BR[Brake fluid above lower mark]
  P[Every ride] --> T[Tyres and tread]
  P --> LI[All lights and horn]
  P --> CO[Throttle, clutch, brakes work]

video.title: JUST GOT YOUR MOTORCYCLE LICENCE??? | Essential Tips for New Riders Singapore

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, weekly and pre-riding checks

summary.tests: Whether you can tell when you are unfit to ride, choose the right gear and posture, and know the pre-ride and weekly check figures.
must_know: About 80% of riding information comes through the eyes; move them every two seconds.
Tired, unwell, angry or on drowsy medicine: do not ride.
Helmet approved and fastened; replace a badly scratched visor.
No sandals, slippers or baggy trousers; bright, tear-resistant clothing.
Tread at least 1.6 mm, chain slack about 20 mm.
Brake free play 15 to 20 mm, clutch free play 10 to 20 mm.
Check engine oil cold and upright on flat ground.
traps: Choosing to ride slowly when tired instead of not riding.
Mixing the brake and clutch free play ranges.
Thinking gloves are a legal requirement: they are recommended; the helmet is the law.

cards.q: About how much riding information comes through your eyes?
cards.a: About 80%.

cards.q: What happens to your field of vision as speed increases?
cards.a: It narrows.

cards.q: What are the three links of the riding chain process?
cards.a: Perception, judgement and reaction.

cards.q: You feel tired before a ride. What should you do?
cards.a: Do not ride.

cards.q: What should you do with a badly scratched visor?
cards.a: Replace it; it causes glare by day and dazzle at night.

cards.q: Why avoid sandals or slippers when riding?
cards.a: Feet can catch on the gear lever, and they give little protection.

cards.q: Where should your feet rest when riding?
cards.a: Arches on the footrests, toes ahead, covering the gear lever and brake pedal.

cards.q: Minimum legal tyre tread depth?
Correct drive chain slack?
cards.a: About 20 mm.

cards.q: Free play for the brake lever and pedal?
cards.a: 15 to 20 mm.

cards.q: Free play for the clutch lever?
cards.a: 10 to 20 mm.

cards.q: How should you check engine oil?
cards.a: Cold engine, motorcycle upright on flat ground, dipstick in without screwing.

cards.q: How should the mirrors be adjusted?
cards.a: Until the tip of your shoulder shows at the lower edge, while seated, not on the main stand.

cards.q: Which lights must you check before riding?
cards.a: Headlamp, hazard lights, turn signals, tail lamp and brake lamp.

flowchart LR
  ST[Need to stop] --> EB[Close throttle for engine braking]

notes.objective: Locate and operate the primary controls
notes.title: Which hand, which foot
notes.gist: Right hand: throttle and front brake. Left hand: clutch. Right foot: rear brake. Left foot: gear pedal.
points: Twist the throttle towards you to accelerate; it springs back to idle.
Clutch lever in means no power to the rear wheel; the biting point is about halfway.
Pull the front brake gently; sudden braking makes the motorcycle wobble and fall.
Pressing the rear brake hard locks the rear wheel.
Gear pedal: lift for a higher gear, press for a lower one, one gear per move. Neutral sits between 1st and 2nd.
Some automatics and electrics have the rear brake lever on the left handlebar.
notes.tip: Before starting: green N lamp lit and the engine stop switch at RUN. Signal right to move off from the kerb.
notes.diagram:
flowchart TB
  RH[Right hand] --> TH[Throttle]
  RH --> FB[Front brake]
  LH[Left hand] --> CL[Clutch]
  RF[Right foot] --> RB[Rear brake]
  LF[Left foot] --> GP[Gear pedal]

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, basic controls

notes.objective: Select gears and use engine braking
notes.title: Gears and engine braking
notes.gist: Lower gears give more power and stronger engine braking. Change down before stopping, before corners and on slopes.
points: 1st gear 0 to 20 km/h for moving off; 2nd 15 to 35 km/h.
Change up at about 3,000 to 4,000 rpm; move off at 2,000 to 3,000 rpm.
Engine braking: throttle closed, gear engaged, clutch out.
Clutch in too early means freewheeling and a longer stopping distance.
Downhill: 3rd on gradual slopes, 2nd on steep slopes, 1st plus footbrake on short steep slopes.
Long footbrake use overheats the brakes and causes fade.
notes.tip: Harsh engine above a gear's range means change up; vibration or knocking below it means change down.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  S[Slope] -->|gradual| G3[3rd gear]
  S -->|steep| G2[2nd gear]
  S -->|short and steep| G1[1st gear plus footbrake]
  G3 --> EB[Engine braking, no fade]
  G2 --> EB
  G1 --> EB

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, speed changing and engine braking

notes.objective: Brake correctly in normal and emergency stops
notes.title: Stopping short without locking up
notes.gist: Use both brakes early with engine braking. In an emergency, brake hard but short of locking the wheels.
points: Stopping distance on a wet road is about twice the dry distance.
If a wheel skids, release the brake and use intermittent braking.
Emergency posture: body straight, eyes ahead, knees grip the tank, firm hands.
Pull the clutch in only as the motorcycle is about to stop.
Emergency brake course: stop within 11 m from about 30 km/h on a wet surface.
Stop about one motorcycle length behind a stationary vehicle.
notes.tip: Never brake and pull in the clutch together straight after closing the throttle: you lose engine braking.
notes.diagram:
flowchart TB
  A[Throttle closed] --> B[Front and rear brakes hard, no lock]
  B --> C{Wheel locked?}
  C -->|yes| D[Release and reapply]
  C -->|no| E[Clutch in just before stop]
  D --> B

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, correct and emergency braking

notes.objective: Corner, climb and handle the circuit courses
notes.title: Cornering, slopes and the circuit
notes.gist: Slow down and change down before a bend, hold steady speed through it, and look where you want to go.
points: Lean with for gradual bends, lean out for sharp low-speed bends, lean in at high speed.
In the bend: steady speed, no brake or clutch. Keep left on right-hand bends.
Centrifugal force grows with speed and sharpness; loads raise the centre of gravity.
Uphill: build speed first; stall on a slope means stamp on the foot brake.
Targets: S course under 11 s, crank and slalom under 6 s, plank 6 s or more.
Look at the next turning point; you ride towards what you stare at.
notes.tip: Going downhill, the ascending vehicle has the right of way.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  B[Before bend: slow, change down] --> I[In bend: steady throttle, no brakes]
  I --> X[Exit: pick up speed, look ahead]

video.title: BBDC S Course | Singapore Motorcycle Riding Test

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, cornering

summary.tests: Whether you know each control, which gear to use when, how engine braking works, and how to brake, corner and climb safely.
must_know: Right hand throttle and front brake, left hand clutch, right foot rear brake, left foot gears.
Lift the gear pedal to go up, press to go down; neutral between 1st and 2nd.
1st gear 0 to 20 km/h, 2nd 15 to 35 km/h.
Engine braking: throttle closed, gear engaged, clutch out.
Use both brakes early; clutch in only just before stopping.
Wet road stopping distance is about double.
In a bend hold steady speed with no brake or clutch.
traps: Pulling the clutch in early, which causes freewheeling.
Locking the wheels in an emergency stop.
Coasting downhill in neutral instead of using a low gear.

cards.q: How do you accelerate with the throttle?
cards.a: Twist it towards you.

cards.q: What is the clutch biting point?
cards.a: About halfway out, where engine power starts to reach the rear wheel.

cards.q: What happens if you press the rear brake pedal too hard?
cards.a: The rear wheel locks and the motorcycle may skid and fall.

cards.q: How do you change to a higher gear?
cards.a: Clutch in, close throttle, lift the gear pedal once, then release the clutch gradually.

cards.q: Where is neutral on a manual motorcycle?
cards.a: Between 1st and 2nd gear.

cards.q: Speed range for first gear?
cards.a: About 0 to 20 km/h.

cards.q: At what rpm is it standard to change up?
cards.a: About 3,000 to 4,000 rpm.

cards.q: What is engine braking?
cards.a: Slowing with the throttle closed, a gear engaged and the clutch not pulled in.

cards.q: What does pulling the clutch in too early cause?
cards.a: Freewheeling and a longer stopping distance.

cards.q: Gear for a steep downhill slope?
cards.a: 2nd or 1st gear.

cards.q: What is the main cause of brake fade?
cards.a: Brakes overheating, for example from long footbrake use downhill.

cards.q: A wheel skids while braking. What should you do?
cards.a: Release the brake, then brake on and off until you stop.

cards.q: Emergency brake course target?
cards.a: Stop within 11 m from about 30 km/h on a wet surface.

cards.q: Which cornering posture suits a sharp bend at low speed?
cards.a: Lean out.

cards.q: Your engine stalls moving off on a slope. First action?
cards.a: Step on the foot brake immediately.

cards.q: Before lifting a fallen motorcycle, what must you do?
cards.a: Switch off the ignition.

notes.objective: Apply give-way rules at junctions and roundabouts
notes.title: Who gives way
notes.gist: Turning traffic gives way to straight-going traffic, and traffic from the right has priority. The rules only say who gives way; nobody owns the right of way.
points: Major road traffic has priority. STOP means a full stop at the line; GIVE WAY means stop only if needed.
Right turns give way to the most traffic.
Roundabout: give way to traffic on your right; do not enter if your exit is blocked; signal left to leave.
Yellow box: never enter and block it, except when turning right waiting for oncoming traffic or held by pedestrians.
U-turn only where a U-turn sign allows it.
Pull out of a minor road when traffic from the right is more than 6 seconds away.
notes.tip: Never assume the other driver will give way just because the rule says so.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[Approach junction] --> B{Sign?}
  B -->|STOP| C[Full stop at line, give way]
  B -->|GIVE WAY| D[Slow, stop if needed]
  B -->|none| E[Give way to the right, turners give way to straight]

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, give-way rules

notes.objective: Keep lane discipline and overtake legally
notes.title: Lanes, lane changes and overtaking
notes.gist: Keep left, use the right lane only to overtake or turn right, signal at least 3 seconds, and do not squeeze between lanes.
points: Two lanes: left for normal riding, right for overtaking and right turns. Three lanes: left for slower vehicles.
Lane change: mirrors, signal 3 seconds, blind spot, adjust speed, move, cancel signal.
Do not ride between two lanes or jump queues by squeezing between lanes.
Overtake on the right. Left only if the vehicle ahead turns right, you turn left, in slow queues, or on one-way streets.
No overtaking near crossings, junctions, bends, crests or double white lines.
Being overtaken: slow down and keep left.
notes.tip: Missed your turn or exit? Carry on to the next one; never stop, reverse or swerve.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  M[Mirrors] --> S[Signal 3 s] --> B[Blind spot] --> A[Adjust speed] --> G[Move smoothly] --> C[Cancel signal]

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, changing lanes and overtaking

notes.objective: Ride expressways correctly
notes.title: Expressway rules
notes.gist: Expressways mean faster traffic and earlier reactions. Some vehicles, including learners, are banned.
points: Most limits are 80 or 90 km/h; the KPE is 70 or 80 km/h. Default road limit is 50 km/h.
Banned: learners, bicycles, e-bikes, motorcycles with sidecars, trishaws and more. Learners only ride it on the supervised Expressway Familiarisation Ride.
Join: signal on the slip road and match speed in the acceleration lane.
Right lane is for overtaking and emergency vehicles; do not exceed the limit to overtake.
Shoulder only for breakdown or accident: riding on it is 6 points.
Leave: signal and move left early, slow on the deceleration lane.
notes.tip: Vehicles with a speed limit of 60 km/h or less must use the left lane of the expressway.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  SL[Slip road: signal] --> AL[Acceleration lane: match speed] --> M[Merge]
  M --> K[Keep steady speed, safe gap]
  K --> EX[Exit: signal left early, slow on deceleration lane]

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, riding on expressways

notes.objective: Read signs, lights and road markings
notes.title: Lights, lines and bus lanes
notes.gist: The BTT signs still apply on the RTT: amber means stop if you safely can, double white lines are never crossed, and bus lanes have set hours.
points: Flashing amber: lights out of order, proceed with caution and give way to the right.
Flickering green arrow: about to end; red arrow: no turn even if clear.
Single yellow line: no parking 7am to 7pm except Sundays and public holidays; double yellow: no parking at all times.
Double yellow zig-zag: no stopping at all times; white zig-zags: crossing ahead.
Normal bus lane Mon to Fri 7.30 to 9.30am and 5 to 8pm; full-day lane has a red line, Mon to Sat 7.30am to 11pm.
No parking within 9 m of a bus stop, 6 m of a junction, 3 m of a hydrant.
notes.tip: During bus lane hours a rider may enter the lane only to avoid a collision.
notes.diagram:
flowchart TB
  AM[Amber] -->|can stop safely| ST[Stop]
  AM -->|too close| GO[Proceed]
  FA[Flashing amber] --> CA[Lights faulty: caution, give way right]

video.title: Explaining Confusing Road Signs That Even Seasoned Drivers Might Not Know

source.title: Basic Theory of Driving, road markings and signals

summary.tests: Whether you can apply the give-way rules, lane discipline, overtaking limits, expressway rules, and the signs, lights and markings shared with the BTT.
must_know: Default speed limit 50 km/h; most expressways 80 or 90 km/h.
Learners and motorcycles with sidecars are banned from expressways; the only learner exception is the Expressway Familiarisation Ride.
Signal at least 3 seconds before turning or changing lanes.
Turning traffic gives way to straight-going traffic; give way to traffic from the right.
Do not enter a yellow box and block it, even on green.
Overtake on the right; never near crossings, junctions, bends or crests.
Amber means stop unless too close to stop safely.
traps: Thinking the give-way rules grant you the right of way.
Squeezing between lanes in a jam: the handbook calls it courting disaster.
Reversing to a missed expressway exit.

cards.q: Default speed limit on Singapore roads?
cards.a: 50 km/h unless signs say otherwise.

cards.q: Speed limits on most expressways?
cards.a: 80 or 90 km/h. The KPE is 70 or 80 km/h.

cards.q: Can a learner ride on the expressway?
cards.a: No, except on the compulsory Expressway Familiarisation Ride after passing the practical.

cards.q: What is the right outermost expressway lane for?
cards.a: Overtaking and emergency vehicles.

cards.q: Going straight at an uncontrolled junction, who do you give way to?
cards.a: Straight-going traffic from the right.

cards.q: Turning right at an uncontrolled junction, who do you give way to?
cards.a: Straight traffic from all directions, right-turners from the right, left-turners from opposite.

cards.q: When may you wait in a yellow box?
cards.a: Turning right waiting for oncoming traffic, or turning and held by crossing pedestrians.

cards.q: Roundabout: who has priority?
cards.a: Traffic on your right already in the roundabout.

cards.q: Where are U-turns allowed?
cards.a: Only where a U-turn sign permits.

cards.q: When may you overtake on the left?
cards.a: Vehicle ahead turning right, you turning left, slow queues, or one-way streets.

cards.q: What does flashing amber mean?
cards.a: Lights out of order: proceed with caution and give way to traffic on the right.

cards.q: Unbroken double white lines?
cards.a: Never cross them. No U-turns or right turns across them, no parking.

cards.q: Normal bus lane hours?
cards.a: Monday to Friday, 7.30 to 9.30am and 5.00 to 8.00pm, not on public holidays.

cards.q: How close to a bus stop may you park?
cards.a: Not within 9 metres.

cards.q: Merging arrows: who goes into the single lane?
cards.a: Alternate vehicles from each lane.

cards.q: You missed your turn. What should you do?
cards.a: Carry on to the next turn. Do not stop suddenly, reverse or swerve.

notes.objective: Keep a safe following distance and know stopping distances
notes.title: The 3, 6 and 12-second rules
notes.gist: Gaps are measured in seconds so they scale with speed. Stopping distance is reaction distance plus braking distance.
points: 3 seconds normally, counted from a fixed point the vehicle ahead passes.
6 seconds when tailgated, behind a heavy vehicle, in poor conditions, loaded or tired.
Scan about 12 seconds ahead; overtaking takes about 12 seconds with the gap.
Average reaction time is 3/4 second.
Dry stopping distance: about 32 m at 50 km/h and 112 m at 100 km/h.
Look ahead at least 3 times your speed in metres: 90 m at 30 km/h.
notes.tip: Being tailgated? Do not speed up or brake-check. Widen the gap ahead to six seconds.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  S[Sees hazard] -->|reaction distance| B[Starts braking]
  B -->|braking distance| X[Stops]
  W[Wet, worn tyres, load] -.->|longer| B

notes.objective: Protect vulnerable road users
notes.title: Pedestrians, cyclists and parked cars
notes.gist: Pedestrians, especially the young and old, are the most vulnerable. Give clear space and expect sudden moves.
points: Children under 15 are impulsive; take care near schools and playgrounds.
White walking stick: slow down, stop and give way.
Gaps: 1 m from pedestrians facing you, 1.5 m from those facing away, 1.5 m from cyclists and moving vehicles.
About 1 m past parked vehicles; watch for doors and smoking exhausts.
At least 0.5 m from fixed obstacles; give way to oncoming traffic if the obstruction is on your side.
A cyclist glancing back may be about to change lanes.
notes.tip: A vehicle slowing near a zebra crossing likely hides a pedestrian. Never overtake it.
notes.diagram:
flowchart TB
  P1[Pedestrian facing you] -->|1 m| G[Minimum gap]
  P2[Pedestrian facing away] -->|1.5 m| G
  C[Cyclist or moving vehicle] -->|1.5 m| G
  F[Fixed obstacle] -->|0.5 m| G

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, pedestrians and cyclists

notes.objective: Avoid the six positions of a two-vehicle crash
notes.title: Six crash positions and their defences
notes.gist: Two-vehicle crashes cause the most deaths and injuries. Each position has a defence: gap, blind spot check, scanning or speed choice.
points: Front: keep the 3-second gap and anticipate sudden stops such as taxis.
Behind: widen your front gap to six seconds to protect the tailgater and you.
Oncoming: read the road, move left, reduce speed, and ride off the road as a last resort.
Side: Know, Slow, Show, Go at intersections.
Overtaking you: match traffic speed, then slow and keep left.
Being overtaken by you: overtaking saves little time here; return left when its front shows in your mirror.
notes.tip: Rear-end the vehicle ahead and you are usually blamed. The gap is your defence.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Y[You] --- F[Front: 3 s gap]
  Y --- B[Behind: 6 s gap]
  Y --- O[Oncoming: move left, slow]
  Y --- S[Side: Know Slow Show Go]
  Y --- OT[Overtaking you: keep left]
  Y --- OV[You overtaking: 12 s scan]

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, six positions of two-vehicle crash

summary.tests: Whether you can keep a safety cushion, judge stopping distances, check blind spots, protect vulnerable road users and defend against the six crash positions.
must_know: 3-second gap normally, 6 seconds in risky conditions, scan 12 seconds ahead.
Stopping distance is reaction plus braking; about 32 m at 50 km/h.
Check mirrors every 5 to 10 seconds; turn your head for blind spots.
Heavy vehicles have blind spots at the sides, rear and front.
Gaps: 1.5 m for cyclists and moving vehicles, 1 m past parked cars, 0.5 m from fixed obstacles.
Head-on defence: read the road, move left, slow down, ride off the road.
Intersections: Know, Slow, Show, Go.
traps: Speeding up when tailgated instead of widening the gap ahead.
Passing a large vehicle on the side it is turning towards.
Assuming the give-way rules mean others will give way to you.

cards.q: How do you apply the 3-second rule?
cards.a: Count three seconds after the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point. Reaching it sooner means too close.

cards.q: When should you use a 6-second gap?
cards.a: When tailgated, behind heavy vehicles, in wet or dark conditions, loaded, or tired.

cards.q: What is the 12-second rule for?
cards.a: Scanning far ahead for hazards and checking there is room to overtake.

cards.q: Average rider reaction time?
cards.a: About three quarters of a second.

cards.q: Approximate dry stopping distance at 50 km/h?
cards.a: About 32 m: 14 m reaction plus 18 m braking.

cards.q: How far ahead should you look at 30 km/h?
cards.a: At least 90 metres, three times your speed.

cards.q: How often should you check your mirrors?
cards.a: Every 5 to 10 seconds.

cards.q: Gap when passing a cyclist?
cards.a: At least 1.5 metres where practicable.

cards.q: Gap when passing parked vehicles?
cards.a: About 1 metre, watching for opening doors.

cards.q: Someone with a white walking stick is crossing. What do you do?
cards.a: Slow down, stop and give way.

cards.q: Name the four head-on collision avoidance rules.
cards.a: Read the road ahead, move left, reduce speed, ride off the road.

cards.q: What are the intersection safety rules?
cards.a: Know, Slow, Show, Go.

cards.q: When should you return left after overtaking?
cards.a: When you see the overtaken vehicle's front in your mirror, after a blind spot check.

cards.q: Which factor causes most traffic accidents?
cards.a: Road users, mainly errors of judgement and riding without due care.

notes.objective: Ride safely in rain, floods and wind
notes.title: Wet roads and aquaplaning
notes.gist: Early rain turns road grime into a slippery film, stopping distance doubles, and fast riding on worn tyres causes aquaplaning.
points: Aquaplaning: a wedge of water lifts the tyre; the steering feels extremely light.
Speed and shallow tread make it worse; even good tyres cannot prevent it.
Slippery when wet: steel plates, manhole covers, painted markings.
If you skid, steer in the direction of the skid and straighten when grip returns.
Floods: low gear, steady throttle, half clutch; then brake on and off to dry the brakes.
Strong wind: slow down, lower gear, firm grip with both hands.
notes.tip: Light rain can be as slippery as the start of a downpour because it does not wash the grime away.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  W[Water on road] --> SP{Fast or worn tread?}
  SP -->|yes| AQ[Aquaplaning, steering light]
  SP -->|no| G[Tyre clears water]
  AQ --> SL[Ease off and slow gently]

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, riding in rainy weather

notes.objective: Use lights correctly by day and night
notes.title: Headlights, glare and night riding
notes.gist: Motorcycles ride with headlights on at all times. At night, dip to avoid dazzling others and never outride your headlight.
points: Headlights on day and night; do not ride if the headlight fails.
Dazzled by oncoming lights: look left, use the road edge, stop if blinded.
Dip when following, when meeting traffic, and as soon as an overtaking vehicle passes.
High beam on poorly lit roads and at blind bends; it reaches about 100 m.
Glare from the sun: sunglasses or a sun visor, and slow down.
Wear bright clothing, a white helmet and reflective gear at night.
notes.tip: Tunnels: headlights on, no overtaking, no horn except emergencies, no stopping unless in trouble.
notes.diagram:
flowchart TB
  N[Night riding] --> D[Dip: following or meeting traffic]
  N --> H[High beam: dark roads, blind bends]
  N --> S[Speed within headlight range, about 100 m]

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, daylight and low lighting

notes.objective: Carry pillions and handle emergencies
notes.title: Pillions, breakdowns and accidents
notes.gist: A pillion changes balance and braking. When things go wrong, keep control first, warn others, then get clear of traffic.
points: No pillion below 10 years old. Pillion sits astride, close, feet always on footrests, leans with you.
Adjust mirrors after the pillion sits; check clothing and tyre pressure.
Front brake failure: rear brake plus engine braking in 2nd. Rear failure: gentle front brake.
Puncture: grip firmly, steer against the pull, brake gently.
Expressway breakdown: shoulder, hazard lights, stand behind guardrails, triangle 20 m or more back.
Accident with no injury: clear the road and settle or inform insurers. With injury: police and ambulance.
notes.tip: In an injury accident, move vehicles only to take someone to hospital, free someone trapped, prevent fire or remove a serious hazard.
notes.diagram:
flowchart LR
  E[Emergency] --> C[Keep control]
  C --> W[Warn: horn and hazard lights]
  W --> S[Move to the side safely]
  S --> X{Injury?}
  X -->|no| N[Clear road, settle or tell insurer]
  X -->|yes| Y[Police and ambulance]

source.title: Riding Theory Booklet, pillion, malfunctions and accidents

summary.tests: Whether you can ride safely in rain, glare and darkness, carry a pillion correctly, and handle breakdowns, failures and accidents.
must_know: Rain doubles stopping distance; early rain is especially slippery.
Aquaplaning makes the steering feel extremely light.
Headlights on day and night; dip when following or meeting traffic.
High beam reaches about 100 m; do not outride it.
No pillion under 10; pillion sits astride with feet on the footrests.
Front brake failure: rear brake plus engine braking in a lower gear.
Always stop after an accident; no-injury cases need not be reported to police.
traps: Braking hard in the rain, which locks the wheels.
Adjusting mirrors before the pillion gets on.
Waiting beside the motorcycle on the expressway shoulder instead of behind the guardrail.

cards.q: Why is the road slippery when rain first starts?
cards.a: Oil, grease and dirt mix with water into a slippery film.

cards.q: Stopping distance in rain compared with dry?
cards.a: About twice as long.

cards.q: How does steering feel when aquaplaning starts?
cards.a: Extremely light.

cards.q: Which wet surfaces are especially slippery?
cards.a: Steel plates, manhole covers and painted road markings.

cards.q: What should you do after riding through a flood?
cards.a: Brake on and off repeatedly to dry the brakes before speeding up.

cards.q: How should you ride in strong wind?
cards.a: Slow down, use a lower gear and grip the handlebar firmly with both hands.

cards.q: Must motorcycle headlights be on during the day?
cards.a: Yes, day and night.

cards.q: Oncoming headlights dazzle you. What do you do?
cards.a: Look to the left, follow the road edge, and stop if blinded.

cards.q: Range of a typical high beam?
cards.a: About 100 metres.

cards.q: Minimum age for a pillion?
cards.a: 10 years.

cards.q: When do you adjust mirrors with a pillion?
cards.a: After the pillion is seated.

cards.q: Front brake fails. What do you do?
cards.a: Hazard lights, rear brake, change down for engine braking, move to the side, switch off.

cards.q: Where do rider and pillion wait after an expressway breakdown?
cards.a: Behind the impact guardrails, clear of the carriageway.

cards.q: Signs of an overheating engine?
cards.a: A sudden increase in engine noise and revolutions.

cards.q: Accident with no injury: must you report it to police?
cards.a: No. Clear the road and settle it or inform your insurers. You must still stop.
